references.text: Here the servant expresses his complete dependence on God as the one who justifies and judges, which reflects Jesus' statement that there is one who seeks and judges.
David's prayer emphasizes that it is the Lord who judges righteously, a theme central to Jesus' claim that there is one who seeks and judges.
In this closely related chapter, Jesus confirms that he can do nothing on his own but judges righteously as he hears, and that he does not seek his own glory.
Jesus warns against those who seek their own glory and contrasts this with the one who seeks the glory of the one who sent him, a direct counterpart to the statement in 8:50.
